svg.title: Recessing the board edge at a breakaway tab
svg.desc: Four close-ups of a board edge at a breakaway tab, drawn to scale. Top row, in the panel: a 2 mm routed slot, cut with a 2 mm router bit so its ends are round, separates the board from the panel frame, and a 5 mm tab bridges it. A row of 0.5 mm holes (mouse bites) runs along the board edge where the tab joins. Left column, without a recess: the holes sit on the straight board edge. Right column, with a recess: the router cuts 1 mm deeper into the board either side of the tab, so the holes sit 1 mm inside the board outline. Bottom row, after breaking: without a recess, a rough stub sticks out past the board outline; with a recess, the stub stays inside it, so the board fits its enclosure without filing.

g.text: 2 mm router bit: round ends, 1 mm radius
0.5 mm holes, 0.1 mm inside the edge
Cut by the same 2 mm bit
Stub sticks out past the outline
Must be filed or sanded off
Board fits its enclosure as is
1.1 mm or more from the edge (see D5)
Example 1 mm; agree it with your fab and assembler
Drawn to scale. Tab, slot and recess sizes are examples.
